newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW profits reinforce rosy outlook.
newsitem.headline: BMW profits reinforce rosy outlook.

text.p: Luxury carmaker BMW said Thursday that its net profit climbed 18.5 percent last year to 820 million marks ($486.4 million) after hot-selling new models boosted sales to a record high.
Bayerische Motoren Werke also said in a brief statement that group profit from ordinary activities climbed to 1.66 billion marks ($984.6 million) marks from 1.37 billion ($812.6 million).

The profit figures, in line with analysts' forecasts, reinforced expectations that the company would post higher profits and sales growth in 1997, despite questions surrounding the future of its mainstay 3-Series model.
"It's a reasonably confident picture for BMW going forward," said John Lawson, car analyst at Salomon Brothers. "Profits will be higher in 1997."
The company will hold its annual press conference next Tuesday, when it will offer its expectations for 1997 and provide a breakdown of the 1996 results.
Analysts attributed the profit growth to three factors -- healthy demand for two recently introduced models, a stronger dollar and probably a smaller loss at BMW's British unit, Rover Group.

BMW announced in January that group sales last year climbed more than 13 percent to a record 52.27 billion marks, largely due to the popularity of its latest 5-Series executive class sedan and the Z3 two-seat roadster, which is made in the United States.
